memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The next day Moses said to the people, 'You have committed a great sin. But now I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.' So Moses went back to the Lord and said, 'Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made themselves gods of gold.'" - Exod 32:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses climbs the mountain again, and this time he goes as a man carrying other people's guilt.

Two things stand out. First, his honesty. He does not minimise: "You have committed a great sin." He says it to their faces and repeats it to God. No spin.

Second, his uncertainty: "perhaps." Moses does not know if atonement is possible. He goes up hoping, not knowing. There is something deeply moving about a man walking into God's presence with no guarantee, simply because he loves these difficult people.

That single word "perhaps" shows us exactly what we have in Christ. Moses could only hope. Jesus did not go to the cross saying "perhaps." He went knowing, and He finished the work. "It is finished" (John 19:30) is the answer to every "perhaps" Moses ever prayed.

The best mediator in the Old Testament could only offer his willingness. Christ offered Himself, and God accepted it fully and forever (Heb 9:26; Heb 10:14).

So when you come to God burdened by real sin — not imagined, not exaggerated, but real — you do not come with "perhaps." You come with certainty, because the atonement has already been made.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you carry others to God in prayer the way Moses did?
2. Are you honest with God about your sin, or do you soften it?
3. What does "It is finished" mean for the guilt you are carrying?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You did not offer a "perhaps" but a finished work. I rest in Your atonement. Amen.
